mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger labor demand is expected to support corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative or flat despite the labor signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of 3% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a bottoming in supply constraints.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops 3% in month t, then rises in month t+1
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 20-day window after the pattern (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (industrial production) of 4% over three months indicates accelerating supply capacity, which is expected to drive positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return during the three-month expansion (rolling IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return via expectations of stronger demand and lower risk premia.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative or flat despite the unemployment signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 3% in the same quarter predict a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual demand weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decrease by ≥3% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in CPIAUCSL (CPI) exceeding 0.5% above the prior month's value in a non-recessionary regime is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to inflation risk premia compression.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% relative to prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or flat despite the CPI spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO growth accelerates from -1% to +2% month-over-month over two months, it predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates supply chain normalization.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth accelerates from -1% to +2% over two months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 5-day window (p > 0.05).
